results.title: MyClaw 3.0: AI Teammates, Features and Pricing - i10X News
results.content:
The AI agent market has a new pitch: stop building agents, hire them. MyClaw, a managed hosting service for the open-source OpenClaw agent, launched version 3.0 on November 18 with what it calls “raised AI teammates with tools built in.” Instead of a blank agent you configure from scratch, users pick a ready-made role such as Chief of Staff or Researcher, choose which agent engine runs it (from Claude Code and Codex to Hermes and OpenClaw) and let it work on a cloud computer that keeps running after the laptop is closed. The launch post passed 1.3 million views on X. Here is what MyClaw 3.0 actually offers, what it costs and what is still unclear.

## Quick Take [...] ### For companies

- Pro: A cloud computer per agent, Slack and Teams access and a built-in data layer could replace a lot of in-house setup.
- Con: Security, compliance and data-handling claims (“Fully private & encrypted”) are self-reported, and Enterprise terms are not public.

## What X is saying

Elvis Saravia (@omarsar0) of DAIR.AI highlighted the harness flexibility:

> Agents shouldn’t be locked into a single harness.  
> MyClaw 3.0 lets you run your agents on Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, or OpenClaw, with context shared across them.  
> Each agent comes with tools and live data sources connected, and keeps running in the cloud after you close the laptop. That makes it easy to pick the right harness for each job. [...] ## Background: from OpenClaw hosting to agent teams

MyClaw started as managed cloud hosting for OpenClaw, the open-source personal AI agent. Its About page describes it as “the easy button for self-hosted AI” and states that MyClaw is “not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to the OpenClaw project or its maintainers.” The service later added Nous Research’s Hermes Agent (see our Hermes Agent review).

Version 3.0 moves up a level, from hosting one agent to assembling a team. It follows a broader industry push toward persistent, role-based agents, from Cognition’s Devin Bots that own goals and lead teams to Microsoft Teams letting agents join as digital teammates.

results.content:
# MyClaw 3.0 bets agents shouldn't pick a harness for you

Questions this post answers

### What is MyClaw 3.0 and how does it work with different AI coding harnesses?

MyClaw 3.0 lets each AI teammate run on Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, or OpenClaw instead of being locked into one harness, carrying shared context across whichever harness is chosen. Teammates work 24/7, can be configured for roles like researcher or engineer, and use a built-in Data Router pulling live data from more than 5,000 sources, including search results and market prices. Comparing agent harnesses before committing is exactly the kind of decision daily.dev helps developers track.

### Did MyClaw originally only support OpenClaw as its agent harness? [...] Yes, MyClaw started as a hosted OpenClaw agent before expanding into a harness-agnostic platform. In version 3.0, OpenClaw became just one option among several, including Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, and Pi, rather than the sole underlying engine. Developers tracking how agent platforms evolve can follow shifts like this one on daily.dev.
